translations.text: A discourse by Saint Epiphanius, Archbishop of Cyprus, on the burial of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And on Joseph of Arimathea, and on Nicodemus, and on the descent of our Lord
to the tombs, which wondrously took place after [?] the saving Passion.
What is this great silence on earth today? What is this great silence and this great stillness?
A great silence, because the King sleeps. The earth was afraid and fell silent,
because God fell asleep in the flesh. God fell asleep in the flesh, and Hades trembled.
God slept for a little while and raised from Hades those who had slept from ages past.
Where now are yesterday’s uproar, voices, and shouting,
raised against Christ by the lawbreakers? Where are the crowds and their ranks, the weapons and clubs?
Where are the kings and priests, and the condemned judges? Where are the torches and swords,
and the countless outcries? Where are the people and their rage, and their unjust toil?
Indeed, truly, the people have truly devised vain things
and foolish things; they stumbled against Christ, the cornerstone,
and were themselves shattered. They hurled themselves against the solid rock,
but their waves dissolved into foam. They struck against the invincible anvil, but were themselves crushed.
They lifted the stone onto the tree, and it came down and killed them. They bound the great Samson, Christ the Sun,
but he shattered the everlasting bonds and destroyed the foreigners and lawbreakers. God the Sun set beneath the earth
and brought deepest darkness upon the Jews. Today there is salvation for those on earth
and for those who have been beneath the earth from ages past. Today there is salvation for the whole world, for all that we see and all that we do not see.
Twofold today is the Lord’s coming, twofold his saving plan, twofold his love for humanity,
twofold his descent and, with it, his humility; twofold his visitation to humanity.
From heaven to earth, from the earth to beneath the earth, God comes.
The gates of Hades open. You who have slept from ages past, rejoice!
You who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, receive the great light!
The Lord is with his servants, God with the dead, Life with those who have died, the innocent with the guilty.
With those in darkness, the unfading light; with the captives, the liberator.
With those in the depths, the one higher than the heavens. Christ is on earth: we have believed.
Christ is among the dead: let us go down with him, so that we may learn the mysteries there.
Let us understand God's mystery, the hidden wonders beneath the earth.
Let us learn how the proclamation has also brought light to those in Hades.
What then? Does God, appearing in Hades, save everyone indiscriminately?
No, but there too, those who believe. Yesterday he was carrying out the works of his saving plan, but today the works of the Master.
Yesterday he was doing the works of the flesh, but today the works of the Lord; yesterday, human works,
but today he reveals divine works. Yesterday he was being struck on the ear,
but today, with divine radiance, he strikes the dwelling of Hades.
Yesterday he was being bound; today he binds the tyrant with bonds that cannot be broken.
Yesterday he was being condemned; today he grants freedom to the condemned.
Yesterday Pilate's servants mocked him; today the gatekeepers of Hades saw him and vanished.
But now hear a loftier account of Christ's suffering. Listen and sing praise.
Listen and glorify him. Listen and proclaim God's great wonders: how the law gives way,
how grace flourishes, how the foreshadowings pass away, how the truth is proclaimed, how the shadow passes away,
how the sun fills the world, how the old law has grown obsolete,
how the new law is made known, how the ancient things have passed away, how new things have blossomed.
Two peoples came to Zion at the time of Christ's suffering: the Jews
and also the Gentiles. Two rulers, Pilate and Herod; two priests,
Annas and Caiaphas, so that both Passovers might take place together, the one ending and Christ's beginning.
Two sacrifices were being offered that evening, since salvation, I say, was coming to the living and the dead.
The Jews bound and slaughtered a lamb, while the Gentiles slaughtered God in the flesh.
The one group looked toward the shadow, while the other came running to the sun and to God.
The one group bound Christ and sent him away, while the Gentiles received him in a different spirit.
But the Jews commemorated the exodus from Egypt.
And those from among the Gentiles proclaimed their deliverance from deception.
And see where: in Zion, the city of the great King, in which he also brought about salvation in the midst
of the earth. Jesus, the Son of God, was made known between two living beings: between the Father and the Spirit,
the two living ones, appearing as life from life, the true life; and between angels
and human beings, being born in a manger; between the two peoples,
lying as the cornerstone; and proclaimed by the Law and the Prophets together;
and appearing on the mountain between Moses and Elijah; and between the two robbers, as God,
revealing himself to the discerning robber; and between the present life and the life to come,
sitting as the eternal Judge; and today appearing between the living and the dead. Again, the power of life is twofold,
for birth and rebirth together are twofold [?]. Hear in these words the events of the twofold birth, and applaud the wonders.
An angel announced his birth to Mary, Christ's mother; an angel announced to Mary Magdalene
his rebirth from the tomb. At night Christ is born in Bethlehem. A cave of stone
is where Christ was born; a cave of stone is where Christ is born anew. At his birth he receives swaddling cloths;
here too he is wrapped in cloths. When he was born, he received myrrh;
at his burial too he receives myrrh and aloes.
There was Joseph, Mary's chaste husband; here is Joseph of Arimathea.
In Bethlehem his birth was in a manger; but in the tomb too there was a place as in a manger. The first
to announce the good news of Christ's birth were shepherds; and the first to announce to everyone
Christ's rebirth from the dead were also shepherds, Christ's disciples. There the angel cried to the virgin, “Rejoice!”
And here Christ, the Angel of Great Counsel, cried to the women, “Rejoice!”
At his first birth, after thirty days Christ entered the earthly Jerusalem, into the temple,
and, as the firstborn, offered two young turtledoves to God. And [?] at his burial from the dead,
after forty days Christ ascended into the heavenly Jerusalem,
from which he had not been separated, into the true Holy of Holies, as the incorruptible firstborn from the dead.
and offering to God the Father two young turtledoves—our soul and our flesh—which he also received,
like another Simeon, God, the Ancient of Days, into his own hands, into his own bosom.
But if you hear these things in a worldly way rather than with faith, the unbroken seals refute you
of the Lord’s burial, of Christ’s tomb. For just as, while the enclosure of virginity was sealed and shut,
Christ was born of the Virgin, so, while the seals of the tomb remained unopened, Christ’s birth took place.
But how Christ, who is life, was once laid in the tomb, and by whom, let us hear from the holy words.
“When evening had come,” it says, “a rich man named Joseph came.” He boldly went in to Pilate
and asked for the body of Jesus. A man went in to a man, asking to receive the God
of mankind. Clay was asking clay to receive the Creator of all;
grass was asking grass to receive the fire of Gehenna; a little drop was asking a drop to receive the abyss.
Who has seen or who has ever heard of a man giving another man the Creator of mankind?
A lawless man promises to give up the righteous one and the Maker of laws. A condemned judge
hands over for burial, as one condemned, the Judge of judges. When evening had come, a man came
named Joseph, truly rich, since he received the whole body of the Lord that had been laid down;
truly rich, since he received Christ’s twofold being from Pilate;
and rich, since he was found worthy to receive the priceless pearl. Truly rich, for he carried a treasury
full of divine riches. For how could he not be rich, having acquired saving life for the whole world?
How could Joseph not be rich, having received as a gift the one who nourishes everyone and rules over all? When evening had come—
for the Sun of Righteousness had already set in Hades—then a rich man named Joseph came
from Arimathea, who had kept himself hidden for fear of the Jews. Nicodemus also came,
the one who had come to Jesus by night. Initiates of hidden mysteries, two secret disciples,
go to hide Jesus in the tomb, the hidden [?] in Hades, to God concealed in the flesh,
teaching through his resurrection. Each surpassed the other in love for God: Nicodemus was generous with myrrh
and aloes, while Joseph was praiseworthy for his boldness toward Pilate.
For he cast aside every fear and boldly went in to Pilate, asking for the body of Jesus.
And when he entered, he began very wisely, so that he would not fail in his cherished purpose.
Therefore he does not begin with any grand words to Pilate, lest he anger him and lose what he is asking for.
Nor does he say to him: Give me the body of Jesus, who darkened the sun a short time ago,
and shattered the rocks, and shook the earth, and opened the tombs,
and tore the curtain of the temple. He says nothing like this to Pilate.
But what does he say? I have come to you, O judge, with a small request, asking for something very small.
Give me for burial the dead body of that man condemned by you: Jesus the Nazarene, Jesus the poor man,
Jesus the homeless man, this Jesus whom you see naked, Jesus the lowly man, Jesus the prisoner,
the bloodied stranger, unknown among strangers, and seen to be neglected by everyone.
Give me this stranger. For what benefit do you gain from the body of this stranger? Give me this Nazarene stranger,
whose country we strangers do not know. Give me this stranger, whose father we strangers do not know.
Give me this stranger, whose home and dwelling we strangers do not know. Give me this stranger,
who has nowhere here to lay his head. Give me this stranger among strangers,
a homeless stranger, who fled from Herod as a stranger from the manger. Give me this stranger,
who fled to Egypt while still in swaddling clothes, who has neither city nor village, neither house nor dwelling nor family
in a foreign land, who has life together with death and holds all things.
Give me, O master, this man hanging naked on the tree, so that I may cover him who covered the nakedness of my body.
Give me this man who is dead and yet is God, so that I may cover him who covered my lawless deeds.
Give me this dead man so that I may bury him who buried my sins in the Jordan.
I plead for a dead man who suffered wrong from everyone, who was betrayed by a friend,
betrayed by a disciple, driven out by his brothers, struck on the ear by his own servants.
I plead for a dead man who was condemned by those he had freed, who was given vinegar to drink as nourishment,
who received a wound from those he had healed,
who was abandoned by his disciples, who was deprived of his own mother. I plead, O Pilate, for a dead man
hanging on a tree. For he has no father on earth, nor any friend now, nor any disciple.
neither relatives nor anyone to bury him, but himself the only-begotten of the One, God in all the world, and no one else.
When Joseph had said these things to Pilate, Pilate ordered that the most holy body of Jesus be given to him.
He came to the place of Golgotha, took God in the flesh down from the tree, and laid
God in the flesh naked upon the ground—yet not naked. And they saw him lying below, who had raised all things on high; and he became almost breathless,
he who is life and breath for all. And they saw without eyes him who had created the many-eyed beings.
And he who is the resurrection of all lay on his back, and God was put to death in the flesh,
he who raises the dead. And the thunder of God's Word was silent in the flesh, and he was lifted by human hands,
he who holds the earth in his hand. Come, then, Joseph, you who asked for him and received him:
do you know whom you received when you approached the cross and took Jesus down?
Do you know whom you carried? If you know whom you hold, you have now become rich.
How, then, do you perform the burial of this divine and awe-inspiring body?
Your love is indeed praiseworthy, but still more praiseworthy is the boldness of your soul.
Come, then, do you not tremble as you carry in your arms him before whom the cherubim tremble? With what fear
do you strip the cloths from that divine flesh? And with what reverence [?] eyes, trembling to look
and to uncover the body of God, who humbled himself willingly? Come, then, tell me, Joseph:
do you bury Jesus facing east as though he were dead, him who is the Sunrise of sunrises?
Come, then, do you close Jesus' eyes with your own fingers as though he were dead,
when he opened the blind man's eyes with his own finger? And do you press shut the mouth
of him who opened the mouth of the man who could not speak clearly? And do you fold the hands
of him who stretched out withered hands? Or do you bind his feet according to the custom for the dead,
when he gave the power to walk to motionless feet? And do you lift onto a bed
him who said to the man whose limbs were paralyzed, 'Take up your bed and walk'?
And do you pour ointment upon the King, who is himself the ointment poured out that healed the whole world?
Come, then, while blood is still flowing from the wound in God's body, do you dare to squeeze it out of him, God who healed the woman with the flow of blood?
Come, then, do you wash with water the body of God, who washed everyone and granted cleansing?
What candles, then, will you light for the true Light,
who has enlightened every person? What funeral songs will you sing
for him who always receives songs from the heavenly powers?
Why, then, do you shed tears as over a dead man,
for him who wept and raised the dead Lazarus? Why, then, do you mourn
for him who gave joy to everyone and took away Eve’s sorrow?
Yet I bless your hands, Joseph, which served and embraced
the divine body while it was still shedding blood—the hands and feet of Jesus.
I bless your hands, which touched God’s side before doubting Thomas did. O faithful and praiseworthy touch!
I bless your lips, which were filled yet never had enough, and pressed themselves to the lips of Jesus,
and were filled with the Holy Spirit from there. I bless your eyes, which pressed themselves to the eyes of Jesus
and received the true light from there. I bless your face,
which pressed itself to God’s face. I bless your shoulders, which carried him who sustains humanity.
I bless your head, which Jesus, the head of all, touched. I bless Joseph and Nicodemus.
For you became more cherubic than the cherubim before them, bearing God in your arms. You became God’s servants before the six-winged ones,
covering God not with wings but with a shroud, and honoring him before whom the cherubim tremble.
You, Joseph and Nicodemus, carry him on your shoulders, while all the ranks of the bodiless beings carry him with them.
Where Joseph and Nicodemus are, have not all the hosts of God’s angels gathered there too?
The cherubim go ahead, the seraphim run before them, and the Thrones carry him with them.
The six-winged ones cover him, and the many-eyed ones tremble, seeing Jesus in the flesh without eyes.
The Powers shelter him, the Dominions sing, and the angelic ranks tremble.
They marvel in terror, discussing it among themselves and saying,
“What is this fearful event, this fear, trembling, and terror? What is this great and marvelous wonder?
God, who above is invisible to us bodiless beings, is seen below as a man, dead and naked.
Joseph and Nicodemus bury without hesitation him before whom the cherubim stand in reverence.”
When did he descend without leaving those on high? How did he descend while remaining within?
How did he come to earth, filling man? How did he descend without anyone noticing?
Being always on high with the Father as God, he had never appeared to us anywhere.
He appeared to human beings as a human being, and at the same time as a lover of mankind. How does the invisible one become visible?
How did the bodiless one take flesh? How did the one beyond suffering accept suffering? How did the Judge stand before a tribunal? How did Life taste death?
How is he who cannot be contained, yet is contained, contained in a tomb? How did he dwell in a tomb without leaving the Father's throne?
How does he enter the gates of the cave without opening the gates of heaven, yet opening the gates of paradise?
And he did not open the gates of virginity, but shattered the gates of Hades.
And he did not open the doors when Thomas was there, but opened the gates of the kingdom to mankind,
while keeping the gates of the tomb and its seals unharmed. How, then, is he counted among the dead, being free even among the dead?
How does the light that cannot be darkened come into the dark places and into the shadows of death? Where is he going? Where is he descending,
he whom death cannot hold? What is the explanation? What is the plan? What is the purpose of his descent
into Hades? Does he perhaps descend to lead up Adam, the prisoner and our fellow servant?
Indeed, he is coming to seek the first-created man, the sheep that was lost.
And he wishes to visit those sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death.
For he is coming to free the captive Adam and the captive Eve from their sufferings, as God
and their son. So let us descend with him! Let us dance with him! Let us leap for joy! Let us
make haste! Let us accompany him! Let us sing praises! Let us bestir ourselves, seeing God's reconciliation with mankind
and the release of prisoners brought about by the good Lord. For the true lover of mankind is coming
to lead out those held prisoner for ages, with courage and great authority,
those dwelling in the tombs, whom the unjust and unconquerable tyrant tormented,
himself tormented by God, who, as an adversary, stole away and gathered those dwelling on high.
There Adam is bound, who was bound before and died before all others,
bound in the lowest depths. There is Abel, who was sacrificed first, the first righteous man,
Christ's shepherd, who became an image of the Shepherd in his unjust slaughter. There is Noah, an image of Christ.
The builder of the great [?] ark of God’s Church, who saved all the hard-hearted nations
from the flood of ungodliness through the dove of the Holy Spirit, and the dark raven, the devil,
having driven him out of it. There was Abraham, Christ’s forefather, the priest,
who offered a godless and immortal sacrifice to God.
There was Isaac, bound long ago by Abraham as a type of Christ.
There was Jacob, sorrowful below in Hades, who had formerly grieved for Joseph above.
There was Joseph, who had been bound in prison in Egypt, as a type of Christ, of the Lord’s imprisonment.
There was Moses, down in the darkness, just as he had been in the basket, down in the darkness.
There was Daniel in the deepest grave of Hades. There was Jeremiah, as though in a pit
full of mud, in the grave of Hades and in the decay of death.
There in the belly of Hades lay Jonah, among the types of Christ, eternal and before all ages,
of Jonah [?], to him who lives forever and for ages of ages, and forever and beyond.
There was David, the forefather of God, from whom Christ was born according to the flesh. And why do I speak of David and Jonah and Solomon?
There was John himself, great and greater than all the prophets,
proclaiming Christ to all those in the graves, as though in a dark womb, a twofold forerunner
and herald to the living and the dead, sent from Herod’s prison
into the prison of souls, to the righteous and unrighteous who had died since the beginning of time.
All the prophets and the righteous, with unceasing prayers, pleaded with God from there,
asking for deliverance from that deeply sorrowful, pitiable domination of the enemy
and from the gloom of the deepest darkness. And one of them said to God:
“From the belly of Hades came my cry; he heard my voice.”
“He cast me into the depths.” “I cried to you, Lord; Lord, hear my voice.” And another said: “Let your face shine, and we shall be saved.”
And another: “You who sit enthroned upon the cherubim, reveal yourself. Stir up your might and come to save us.”
And another: “Let your mercies quickly come to meet us, Lord.” And another: “Deliver my soul from the deepest Hades.”
And another: “Lord, you have brought my soul up from Hades.”
And another: “Do not abandon my soul in Hades.” And another: “Let my life rise from corruption
to you, O Lord my God.” Consider: not only to those who died in his time and after him
did he proclaim his love for humanity, but also to those held captive by Hades before his coming,
and to those sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death. Therefore, human beings who were in the flesh
God the Word visited in flesh endowed with a soul; but souls that were without flesh
he enlightened in Hades with his divine and most pure soul, which from the body,
but not from the Godhead, was separated. Therefore let us make haste and go in thought into Hades,
so that we may see how there, at that time, with mighty power, he utterly subdues
the tyranny of the one who held sway, and with his undying radiance [?], the warriors,
the ranks of armies, he binds without hands, removing the doors of the abyss from their place.
And Christ shattered the gates, which were not made of wood, with the cross, and crushed the nails and the everlasting bars.
And having broken [?], with his bonds and his own hands, the iron chains that could not be loosened for him
he melted like wax. And with the spear that pierced God’s side,
he pierced the tyrant’s bodiless heart. There he shattered his power with his bow,
when with his divine hands he bent the cross like a bow, using his bonds as a bowstring.
Therefore, if you follow Christ in silence, you now see when he bound the tyrant,
where he impaled his head, how he demolished his prisons, how he led out the prisoners, how he ripped open the serpent, and where
he hung the serpent; how he freed Adam, how he raised Eve, and how he tore down the dividing wall;
and where he condemned the fierce serpent, how he established his invincible victories, where he put death to death,
and how he destroyed corruption and restored humanity to its original sovereign dignity.
He who yesterday declined the sovereign legion of angels, saying to Peter,
“I can now bring before me more than twelve legions of angels,”
today, in a manner worthy of God, and at once courageously and sovereignly,
descends against Hades and against death, and against the tyrant of death by means of death. Immortal
bodiless warriors and invisible ranks, not to God [?], not merely legions.
but myriads upon myriads and thousands upon thousands, [?] angels and archangels,
authorities, principalities, dominions, powers, and thrones, the six-winged and many-eyed beings
of the heavenly ranks, escorting him as their own Lord and King, bringing gifts
and singing praise to Christ—not giving him help in battle, for this is not fitting for God.
For what help does Christ need? Rather, out of duty and honor, with love, they continually stand before their own Lord,
having been granted the right to stand before God at all times, some as armed guards, and likewise as spearmen,
swift for the Lord’s battle, set in motion by a mere nod with divine speed, together racing to outstrip one another,
carrying out the commands in action, [?], and with victory
arrayed and armed against enemies and tyrants. Therefore they also descended then, running together
and following God and the Lord to the tombs and to places deeper than all the earth,
the underground dwellings of those dead from ages past, to bring out those in chains who had slept from ages past.
And when the gates and the sunless dwellings of Hades, its dwellings and prisons,
its storehouses and caves, were reached by God’s visitation and his radiant coming,
Gabriel the chief commander goes ahead of them all, bringing people good news of joy, as is his custom.
And with a mighty utterance, archangelic and radiant like a commander’s,
and lionlike toward the opposing powers, he says in a loud voice, “Lift up your gates, you princes!”
With them Michael cries, “And be lifted up, you everlasting gates!” Then the powers also said,
“Stand aside, you lawless gatekeepers!” Likewise the principalities, with authority:
“Be shattered, you unbreakable iron bonds!” And another: “Be ashamed, you hostile adversaries!”
And another: “Be afraid, you lawless tyrants!” And as they stand beside the valiant King,
arraying themselves royally for battle and conquering, a certain terror and trembling,
together with confusion and dreadful fear, falls upon the gates of the invincible ruler.
Likewise, at that wondrous coming of Christ into Hades, into the lowest regions, suddenly from above there came
a flash [?] darkness, in the faces of the opposing powers of Hades, as they heard a certain thunderous voice shouting,
and warriors commanding and saying, “Lift up your gates, you princes! Lift up the gates!”
For do not open them, but lift them out from their very foundations. Uproot them; remove them.
Let them no longer be shut. Lift up your gates, you princes.
Not because the Lord who has come is unable to enter when the gates are shut, whenever he commands,
but because, as your master, he commands you as poor slaves to lift up the eternal gates,
and to remove and shatter them. Therefore, not to your peoples, but to those who think themselves rulers,
he gives the command, saying, “Lift up your gates, you princes”—yet you are not rulers over anyone else.
For even though until now you have wickedly ruled over those who have died since the beginning of time, from now on you shall no longer rule over them.
But neither over others nor over you—nor even over your very selves—will you be rulers. Lift up the gates.
For Christ, the heavenly door, has come. Make a path for him who has entered the farthest west.
The Lord is his name, and to the Lord belong the ways out through the gates of death.
You made entrances into death, but he himself will make an exit. He has come.
Therefore lift up your gates, you princes; lift them up and do not delay. Lift them up quickly; lift them up and do not wait.
But if you intend to delay, he commands the gates themselves to rise on their own, without any hand touching them. Rise up, you gates
that are eternal. At once the powers cried out.
At once the gates rose up. At once the iron bonds and bars were shattered. At once the locks fell away.
At once the foundations of the prison shook. At once the hostile powers took to flight,
pushing one another, stumbling over one another, and telling one another to flee.
They were frightened and shaken. They were terrified and thrown into confusion. They grew pale and stood together.
They marveled; together they were bewildered and trembled. One of them stood gaping.
Another covered his face with his knees, while another gasped face down, and another grew stiff as though dead.
Another was gripped by terror and lay pale.
Another [?] in the inner hiding places. For there Christ then struck down
the heads of the mighty in terror. There it trembled within him. There they loosened their bridles, saying,
“Who is this King of glory? Who is this, who performs such great wonders here among so many?
Who is this King of glory, who now does in Hades what has never happened in Hades before?”
Who is this who leads out of here those who have been bound since the beginning of time?
Who is this who has shattered our invincible dominion and might?
The Lord’s powers answered them, saying:
Do you wish to know who this King of Glory is? The Lord, mighty and strong.
The Lord, strong and mighty and invincible in battle. He is the one who cast
you out of the heavenly places and sent you to the earth. O wretched, lawless tormentors!
He is the very one who crushed, in the waters of the Jordan,
the heads of your serpents. He is the very one who exposed you through the cross and made a spectacle of you
and weakened your sinews. He is the very one who bound you and cast you into darkness
and sent you into the abyss. He is the very one who sends you into eternal fire
and into Gehenna. Therefore do not delay or wait, but get moving and bring out the prisoners whom you have swallowed up until now.
For your dominion has already been shattered; your tyranny has already ceased.
How violently your raging has been shattered! Your pride has been utterly brought low.
Your strength has failed and perished. These things the Lord’s powers said to the opposing powers.
At the same time they hurried to act. Some tore down the prisons to their very foundations.
Others pursued the opposing powers from the outer chambers,
as they fled into the inner ones. Still others searched the underground storehouses and hiding places
and caves, running about. And some, from different places, brought prisoners to the Lord, one after another.
Others bound the tormentor, while still others released those who had been bound for ages.
Others hurried to serve, and some ran ahead of Christ as he entered within.
Others stood before him as God and King and Conqueror. While these things were happening in this way,
and even greater things than these were taking place in Hades, and everyone was speaking
and trembling at the Lord’s coming,
the lowest depths themselves wished to descend into still lower depths. That Adam—
that Adam, who had been bound before all other people, in the innermost place of all.
Held bound very securely, he heard the Lord’s feet approaching the prisoners.
And he recognized the sound of the one walking in the prison, and turned toward all those who were with him,
bound since the beginning of time, and said, “I hear the footsteps of someone coming toward us.
And if he has indeed chosen to come here, we shall be freed from our bonds. If we truly see him with us,
we shall be delivered from our bonds.” While Adam was saying these and similar things
to all the prisoners who were with him, the Lord entered where they were,
holding the victorious weapon of the cross. When Adam, the first to be created, saw him,
he struck his breast in awe and cried out to all who had been sleeping since the beginning of time,
and said, “My Lord is with everyone!” And Christ answered Adam,
“And with your spirit.” And taking him by the hand, he raised him up, saying,
“Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.
I am your God, who for your sake became your son. Now I speak and with authority command the prisoners,
‘Come out!’ And to those in darkness, ‘Be enlightened!’ And to those lying down, ‘Arise!’
I command you: awake, sleeper! For I did not create you to be bound in Hades.
Rise from the dead, for I am the life of humankind. Arise, my creation!
Arise, my likeness, made in my image! Arise, let us go from here.
For you are in me and I am in you; we are one undivided body.
For your sake I, your God, became your son. For your sake I, who am Lord, took on the form
of you, a slave. For your sake I, who am above the heavens, came to earth and beneath the earth.
For your sake, a human being, I became like a human being without help, free even among the dead.
For your sake, who left the garden, I was handed over to the Jews from a garden,
and in a garden I was condemned. See the spitting on my face, which I endured for your sake,
to restore you to your first breath of life. See the blows on my cheeks, which I endured
to restore your disfigured likeness to its original image. See the wounds on my shoulders, which I endured
to cast off the burden of your sins that lies upon your shoulders. See my hands nailed fast.
I who stretched out my hands on the tree for good, for your sake, who stretched out your hands toward the tree for evil.
Look at my feet, nailed and fastened to the tree for the sake of your feet,
which ran wickedly toward the tree on the sixth day. Your condemnation took place on the sixth day.
And I brought about your judgment and the opening of paradise. For your sake I tasted gall,
to heal you of the bitter pleasure of that sweet food. I tasted vinegar,
to destroy the sour and terrible cup of your death.
And I accepted the sponge to wash away the written record of your sin. I also accepted the reed,
to write a grant of freedom for the human race. I fell asleep on the cross and was pierced in the side with a spear,
for your sake, who fell asleep in paradise and brought Eve out of your side. My side has healed
the pain of your side. My sleep will bring you out of the sleep of death.
My spear has stopped the spear that turns against you. Therefore arise,
and go from here. I led you out of the land of paradise.
I am now placing you in paradise, but on a heavenly throne. I barred you from the tree that was an image of life.
But now I, who am wholly life, have shared myself with you. I commanded the cherubim to guard you as servants; I will make the cherubim bow down to you. You hid from God because you were naked.
But now you have hidden the naked God within yourself. You clothed yourself in a shameful garment of skin.
But I, God, clothed myself in your flesh, in a garment of skin.
Therefore arise and go from here, from decay to incorruptibility,
from death to life. Arise and go from here,
from darkness into eternal light. Arise and go from here, from suffering to joy.
Arise and go from here, from slavery to freedom, from prison to the Jerusalem above,
from chains to God, from pain to the food of paradise, from earth to heaven.
For this is why I died and rose again: to rule over both the living and the dead.
Therefore arise and go, for the heavenly Father awaits the lost sheep.
The ninety-nine angelic sheep await their fellow servant Adam:
when will he rise, when will he ascend and return to God? The cherubic throne has been made ready.
The bearers are eager. Alternatively: ready. The table has been prepared. The food is ready. Eternal shelters and dwellings.
The treasures of good things have been opened. The kingdom of heaven was prepared before the ages—things that no eye has seen and no ear has heard,
good things that have not entered the human heart await man. These and similar
things the Lord was saying, and Adam, who was in him, rises together with him.
And he raises with him, when [?] also many bodies of the saints who had died from ages past
rose, proclaiming the Lord’s resurrection on the third day. Let us receive it with joy
and see it and embrace it, rejoicing with the angels, celebrating with the archangels,
and together glorifying Christ, who has raised us from decay.
To him be glory and power, with the Father who has no beginning
and the most holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
